name: Congenital Peritoneal Encapsulation

criteria.description: Identification of an accessory peritoneal membrane encapsulating the small intestine on imaging or surgery
Clinical signs and symptoms consistent with intermittent or acute small bowel obstruction
Exclusion of secondary causes of encapsulating peritonitis such as sclerosing encapsulating peritonitis
Histopathological confirmation of normal peritoneal tissue without fibrosis or inflammation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of encapsulating membrane visualized during surgery or imaging with clinical signs of small bowel obstruction and exclusion of secondary causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is often made intraoperatively due to rarity and nonspecific clinical presentation.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Encapsulation of small intestine by accessory peritoneal membrane
pathognomonic.notes: Typically identified intraoperatively or on imaging
searchTerms: small intestine wrapped by extra membrane

pathognomonic.notes: Recurrent episodes due to mechanical constriction

common.symptomName: Nausea and vomiting associated with obstruction
searchTerms: throwing up due to bowel obstruction

occasional.symptomName: Weight loss secondary to chronic obstruction
occasional.notes: Due to malabsorption or reduced intake
searchTerms: weight loss from chronic bowel blockage
poor weight gain from intestinal problems

occasional.notes: May indicate secondary inflammation or complication

rare.symptomName: Peritonitis due to bowel ischemia or perforation
searchTerms: inflamed abdomen due to bowel ischemia
low blood pressure due to bowel necrosis

laboratory: Non-specific inflammatory markers may be mildly elevated
Normal routine blood tests unless complications occur
imaging: CT scan showing small bowel encapsulated by thin accessory peritoneal membrane
Barium studies demonstrating clustering of small bowel loops
Ultrasound may show encapsulated bowel loops
genetic: No known genetic mutations associated; considered a congenital anomaly
other: Intraoperative finding of accessory peritoneal sac encapsulating small intestine
Histopathology showing normal peritoneal tissue without fibrosis or inflammation

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of thick fibrotic peritoneal membrane
History of peritoneal dialysis or peritonitis
Entrapment of bowel loops through a mesenteric or peritoneal defect

redFlags: Signs of acute small bowel obstruction with severe abdominal pain
Evidence of bowel ischemia or perforation
references: Al-Taan O, et al. Congenital peritoneal encapsulation: a rare cause of small bowel obstruction. Int J Surg Case Rep. 2016;28:208-211.
Singh S, et al. Congenital peritoneal encapsulation: a rare cause of intestinal obstruction. J Clin Diagn Res. 2017;11(2):PD01-PD02.
